articles.impactReason: The outbreak carries major regional public-health consequences, while individual transmission routes require careful verification.
articles.title: Congo's Ebola outbreak exceeds 10,000 cases, with 4,887 deaths reported
articles.dek: The 27 October health tally lists 10,060 confirmed infections; cross-border developments need separate country-level counts.
articles.summary: On 27 October, the Democratic Republic of Congo's public-health institute reported 10,060 confirmed Ebola cases and 4,887 deaths. This is a new update to the Bundibugyo-virus outbreak first announced in May 2026. Reuters and Associated Press separately reported the milestone, which should not be conflated with ECDC's earlier 9,964-case count as of 24 October.
body: On 27 October, the Democratic Republic of Congo's public-health institute reported 10,060 confirmed Ebola cases and 4,887 deaths. This is a new update to the Bundibugyo-virus outbreak first announced in May 2026. Reuters and Associated Press separately reported the milestone, which should not be conflated with ECDC's earlier 9,964-case count as of 24 October.

These figures place the current outbreak above Congo's 2018–2020 epidemic in reported size and deaths and, Reuters says, second worldwide only to West Africa's 2014–2016 outbreak. Such historical comparisons depend on the categories and reporting periods used: confirmed cases, reported deaths and surveillance dates. A crude death-to-case ratio is not an individual patient's survival probability.

Reports have also emerged outside Congo, including cases in Kenya and an investigation into an infection in Nigeria. How the Nigerian patient, who reportedly did not travel to Congo, became infected remains unresolved; assigning a specific route of exposure would be speculative. Countries update their bulletins at different times and with different surveillance criteria.

The rising toll underscores the value of timely diagnosis, safe isolation, contact tracing and protection for health workers. Violence against health staff reported in northeastern Congo may complicate those activities, but its numerical contribution to the outbreak's course has not been measured. Further assessments depend on public-health bulletins and epidemiological investigations.
facts: Congo's 27 October report lists 10,060 confirmed cases and 4,887 deaths.
The outbreak involves the Bundibugyo Ebola virus.
perspectives: Public-health authorities emphasise containment and contact surveillance.
unknowns: Transmission chains for some cases outside Congo and the effects of violence against health workers remain unresolved.

questions.question: What does the relationship between 10,060 cases and 4,887 deaths in Congo represent?
questions.answer: It is a cumulative ratio of reported deaths to confirmed cases at the bulletin date, not an individual's prognosis; diagnosis delays, reporting and patients' circumstances differ.

questions.question: Why do cases reported in Kenya and Nigeria require separate epidemiological investigations?
questions.answer: Geographical proximity does not prove one transmission chain. Contact histories, travel, clinical data and, when available, genomic comparisons are needed to link particular infections.

articles.impactReason: The political outcome could influence regional security and diplomacy; high turnout is documented but does not identify a winner.
articles.title: Israel votes: 55.7% turnout by 4 p.m., no final result yet
articles.dek: Election officials report unusually high participation, but any government needs at least 61 of 120 seats.
articles.summary: On Tuesday 27 October Israelis are voting for a new Knesset after years marked by war and deep political division. The Central Elections Committee reported 55.7% turnout by 4 p.m. local time, compared with 47.5% at the equivalent point in 2022. The Times of Israel reported the figure, while the Guardian and Reuters separately covered the election. This is an interim turnout update, not the final participation rate.
body: On Tuesday 27 October Israelis are voting for a new Knesset after years marked by war and deep political division. The Central Elections Committee reported 55.7% turnout by 4 p.m. local time, compared with 47.5% at the equivalent point in 2022. The Times of Israel reported the figure, while the Guardian and Reuters separately covered the election. This is an interim turnout update, not the final participation rate.

Polling stations operate from 7 a.m. until 10 p.m. local time, and eligible voters arriving before closure may still cast their ballots. The contest pits Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud and allies against an opposition field including former army chief Gadi Eisenkot. Pre-election polling suggested a close contest, but projections from earlier surveys are not seats already won.

The Knesset has 120 members, and forming a government normally requires support from at least 61 of them. Parties failing to clear the national 3.25% threshold win no seats, which can substantially affect distribution among blocs. Differences in turnout between communities therefore matter even without a dramatic vote shift within any one party.

During voting, politicians made allegations about irregularities and efforts to influence voters. The election committee said it had seen no indication of widespread problems; campaign allegations are not judicial findings. Exit polls and vote counts only follow poll closure, while coalition formation may require further negotiations.
facts: Turnout reported at 4 p.m. local time on 27 October was 55.7%.
The Knesset has 120 seats and the national electoral threshold is 3.25%.
perspectives: Netanyahu and rivals frame the election as decisive for Israel's security and political direction.
Election officials distinguish political allegations from documented irregularities.
unknowns: Final vote totals, seat allocation and potential governing coalitions were not determined at writing time.

questions.question: Why can high Israeli turnout change the distribution of 120 Knesset seats?
questions.answer: Parties must pass the nationwide 3.25% threshold to enter parliament. Different communities' participation can determine which lists qualify and how seats are distributed among coalition blocs.

questions.question: Can the 55.7% turnout at 4 p.m. determine who governs Israel?
questions.answer: It measures participation up to that hour, not votes for parties. Governing requires 61 seats, and negotiations may still be necessary after final results.

articles.impactReason: Civilian harm in the capital carries significant security and diplomatic consequences, while exact counts and intent need attribution.
articles.title: New missile strikes hit Kyiv on 26 October, damaging civilian sites
articles.dek: Reported casualties changed across updates; this strike is distinct from the 22 October attack.
articles.summary: During the evening of Monday 26 October, Russian missiles struck several locations in Kyiv, according to Ukrainian officials and reporting from Reuters and the Guardian. Mayor Vitali Klitschko reported explosions and damage near health facilities and transport infrastructure; President Volodymyr Zelenskyy described an impact on university grounds. These events concern the 26 October strike, not the separate 22 October attack already in the archive.
body: During the evening of Monday 26 October, Russian missiles struck several locations in Kyiv, according to Ukrainian officials and reporting from Reuters and the Guardian. Mayor Vitali Klitschko reported explosions and damage near health facilities and transport infrastructure; President Volodymyr Zelenskyy described an impact on university grounds. These events concern the 26 October strike, not the separate 22 October attack already in the archive.

Initial reports described at least one person killed and several injured. The Guardian cited eight injured in its overnight update, while a later Reuters account referred to as many as ten. Differences may reflect the timing of casualty verification and should not be merged into a single count falsely attributed to both outlets.

Reports identify university grounds and healthcare facilities among the damaged locations. Zelenskyy said the missiles hit densely populated places without nearby military installations. That is the Ukrainian president's statement; identifying the intended targets and detailed circumstances would require technical evidence and independent investigation.

The strike occurred hours before a limited ceasefire began around Oleshky in southern Ukraine. The two developments are not contradictory: the negotiated pause applies to a local area, not the whole country. Distinguishing geographical scope is essential when interpreting simultaneous reports about war and diplomacy.
facts: The 26 October Kyiv strike is separate from the 22 October bombardments.
Reports describe at least one death and differing subsequent injury counts.
perspectives: Ukraine's government condemns strikes on civilian locations; Moscow's intended military rationale is not established in the reviewed accounts.
unknowns: Final injury totals, intended targets and independent damage assessments remain unresolved.

questions.question: Why do Guardian and Reuters give different injury numbers for the Kyiv strike?
questions.answer: Their updates appeared at different times after the attack: the Guardian reported eight injured, while a Reuters update referred to up to ten. Rescue work and verification can change early counts.

questions.question: Did the Oleshky ceasefire cover the 26 October attacks on Kyiv?
questions.answer: The announced agreement applied to a humanitarian operation around Oleshky in the Kherson region. It was not a countrywide ceasefire covering all of Ukraine.

articles.impactReason: The stock and currency shock has immediate financial consequences in South America's largest market.
articles.title: Brazil's Ibovespa falls 13.88% on 26 October, triggering trading halt
articles.dek: Markets reacted to Lula's re-election; the session low must be distinguished from the closing index.
articles.summary: Brazilian stocks experienced a turbulent Monday, 26 October, after Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won re-election in the previous day's presidential run-off. Agência Brasil and Folha de S.Paulo report a 13.88% closing fall for the Ibovespa, to roughly 176,608 points. The new development is the market response, not a repeat of the election result already covered.
body: Brazilian stocks experienced a turbulent Monday, 26 October, after Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won re-election in the previous day's presidential run-off. Agência Brasil and Folha de S.Paulo report a 13.88% closing fall for the Ibovespa, to roughly 176,608 points. The new development is the market response, not a repeat of the election result already covered.

Trading was temporarily suspended by a circuit breaker after the index fell more than 17% at its intraday low, around 169,516 points. The final decline was smaller than the steepest morning loss. A headline citing a 17% drop may therefore describe the worst point in the session rather than the closing result.

The US dollar surged against the real. Agência Brasil reported an 8.21% increase to 5.403 reais per dollar; some other market accounts give slightly different figures depending on the timestamp or quotation convention. Investors reassessed their expectations for fiscal policy after an election outcome that differed from many market positions.

Volatility can affect financing costs for companies and households, but a single trading day does not predict Brazil's economic trajectory. Brazilian reporting described Treasury operations in the bond market. The medium-term picture will depend on government decisions, investor confidence, interest rates and later economic data.
facts: The Ibovespa closed on 26 October at about 176,608 points, down 13.88%.
A circuit breaker paused trading during an intraday decline exceeding 17%.
perspectives: Analysts link selling to a reassessment of fiscal expectations after the vote.
unknowns: Individual stock moves cannot all be attributed solely to the election, and the duration of volatility is unknown.

questions.question: What did the circuit breaker do during the Ibovespa plunge?
questions.answer: It temporarily suspended trading after a sharp market fall, aiming to limit disorderly transactions. Trading later resumed, and the index closed down 13.88%.

questions.question: Why isn't the drop of more than 17% the final Brazilian stock-market figure?
questions.answer: That was the worst intraday decline, while the 13.88% loss refers to the closing level after prices changed later in the session.

articles.impactReason: A local pause may reduce risk for thousands of isolated civilians without changing fighting elsewhere in Ukraine.
articles.title: Russia and Ukraine confirm local Oleshky humanitarian ceasefire has begun
articles.dek: The 27 October pause aims to enable aid and evacuations in an occupied town; fighting continues elsewhere.
articles.summary: Early on 27 October, Russia and Ukraine said a local ceasefire had begun around Oleshky, a Russian-occupied town in the Kherson region. Reuters obtained confirmations from Russia's defence ministry and Ukrainian ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets; Deutsche Welle also covered the start. Implementation is the new development beyond the agreement announced on 23 October.
body: Early on 27 October, Russia and Ukraine said a local ceasefire had begun around Oleshky, a Russian-occupied town in the Kherson region. Reuters obtained confirmations from Russia's defence ministry and Ukrainian ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets; Deutsche Welle also covered the start. Implementation is the new development beyond the agreement announced on 23 October.

The pause is meant to allow deliveries of food, water and medicines, and evacuation of residents isolated by fighting, flooding and mines. Lubinets explained that land routes need demining before convoys and emergency vehicles can reach civilians. Authorities estimate roughly 2,000 people remain, but no independently verified house-by-house count is available.

According to published statements, Russia's ministry said it had halted shelling towards Kherson at the agreed time, while Lubinets said Ukraine was observing its commitments. Those are claims by the respective parties, not continuous independent monitoring of every area. Earlier competing accusations about the causes of humanitarian blockages remain disputed.

The same day's reports describe new attacks elsewhere in Ukraine, including Kyiv. The arrangement is geographically limited and does not end the war or prove every aid corridor is operational. Its humanitarian value will depend on verifiable deliveries and safe evacuations, not simply on the announced start time.
facts: Both sides confirmed the local pause had begun on 27 October.
The plan aims to deliver supplies and evacuate civilians from Oleshky.
perspectives: Lubinets emphasises that access routes must be cleared of mines before aid can be delivered.
Russian officials say they halted fire in the designated sector.
unknowns: The amount of aid delivered, evacuation totals and on-the-ground verification arrangements remain unconfirmed.

questions.question: Why is demining central to the Oleshky ceasefire?
questions.answer: Access roads contain mines and explosive hazards. Even when shelling stops, humanitarian vehicles cannot safely reach residents until usable routes are cleared.

questions.question: How can the ceasefire's announced start be distinguished from humanitarian success?
questions.answer: Both parties said the pause began. Success requires actual deliveries of food, water and medicines and safe evacuations, ideally independently verified.

articles.impactReason: The allegations affect EU and NATO industrial security, but criminal proceedings remain unresolved.
articles.title: Romanian investigators link Brașov industrial fire to alleged Russia-coordinated network
articles.dek: On 26 October agencies detailed their case over the 14 September blaze and three suspects; claims are not convictions.
articles.summary: On 26 October Romania's intelligence service, SRI, and organised-crime prosecutors, DIICOT, disclosed new findings on a fire that broke out on 14 September at the Carfil industrial platform in Brașov. Officials allege the incident was organised by a sabotage network coordinated from Russia. Reuters, Agerpres and Romania Insider covered the announcement, which does not amount to a final criminal conviction.
body: On 26 October Romania's intelligence service, SRI, and organised-crime prosecutors, DIICOT, disclosed new findings on a fire that broke out on 14 September at the Carfil industrial platform in Brașov. Officials allege the incident was organised by a sabotage network coordinated from Russia. Reuters, Agerpres and Romania Insider covered the announcement, which does not amount to a final criminal conviction.

DIICOT says the investigation concerns three foreign EU residents, two Belarusian nationals and one Ukrainian. Two were located and remanded in custody in Germany, while a third was located in Poland. Romanian courts issued European arrest warrants and authorities are pursuing extradition. The suspects' nationalities do not by themselves establish who directed the operation.

The site lies close to a subsidiary of state-owned weapons group ROMARM. Intelligence officials allege the network was also given other military and industrial targets across the region. SRI described a recruitment pattern beginning with paid small tasks and potentially escalating through coercion. Complete technical evidence, communications and case files have not been made public.

The case sits within Romanian allegations of hybrid operations against European industrial and defence infrastructure. Moscow has broadly denied similar sabotage accusations, so officials' claims must be distinguished from legally established responsibility. Public interest lies in industrial protection, cross-border judicial cooperation and the quality of evidence.
facts: SRI and DIICOT reported on 26 October about the 14 September Brașov fire.
Romanian authorities say three people are subject to European arrest warrants.
perspectives: Romania's intelligence service attributes coordination of the alleged network to actors in Russia.
Russia broadly denies allegations of sabotage campaigns against European countries.
unknowns: Court proceedings are not complete and the full evidence on any chain of command is not publicly available.

questions.question: What do European arrest warrants do in the Brașov Carfil case?
questions.answer: They let Romanian authorities request the transfer of suspects found in other EU countries for criminal proceedings. An arrest warrant is not a conviction.

questions.question: Why doesn't the SRI announcement conclusively prove Russia's involvement?
questions.answer: It states investigators' findings and intelligence attribution. Criminal responsibility requires judicial evaluation of evidence, and the complete case record is not public.

articles.impactReason: The talks involve major regional security actors, but the concluding statement is preliminary and political.
articles.title: Iran, Saudi Arabia, Türkiye and Pakistan agree to continue regional talks
articles.dek: After the 26 October Tehran meeting, officials announced further security dialogue, not a peace treaty.
articles.summary: Senior delegations from Saudi Arabia, Türkiye and Pakistan met Iranian officials in Tehran on 26 October. The meeting came amid Houthi attacks towards Saudi Arabia and tensions involving Iran, the United States and Israel. Associated Press and Reuters independently reported the participants and stated aims of the talks.
body: Senior delegations from Saudi Arabia, Türkiye and Pakistan met Iranian officials in Tehran on 26 October. The meeting came amid Houthi attacks towards Saudi Arabia and tensions involving Iran, the United States and Israel. Associated Press and Reuters independently reported the participants and stated aims of the talks.

The delegations included Saudi Defence Minister Khalid bin Salman, Pakistani army chief Asim Munir and Turkish intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalın, according to official accounts. Iran hosted the discussions, and Iranian state media reported a closing statement supporting continued cooperation on peace and security. IranWire examined the reported statement.

The gathering was the first high-level joint contact since Saudi Arabia, Türkiye and Pakistan signed their mutual-defence agreement in Mecca in August. That three-country pact does not make Iran a member. Accounts of possible Pakistani proposals to Washington and Tehran are attributed to officials and cannot be treated as published diplomatic agreements.

IranWire noted that as of 27 October the other three participating governments had not issued independent accounts of the summit's conclusions. There is therefore no evidence of a binding timetable, regional ceasefire or settlement over the Strait of Hormuz. The immediate significance lies in retaining channels for diplomacy among governments under strain.
facts: The Tehran meeting took place on 26 October with representatives of four states.
A statement reported by Iranian authorities indicates an intention to continue dialogue.
perspectives: Saudi Arabia presents the initiative as an effort to avert further military escalation.
Iranian officials emphasise the value of regional cooperation.
unknowns: Detailed terms, future meeting dates and separate confirmation by all delegations have not been made public.

questions.question: How is the Tehran summit related to the Mecca defence agreement?
questions.answer: Saudi Arabia, Türkiye and Pakistan signed the August pact and joined the talks with Iran. The summit did not turn that three-country pact into a four-country treaty.

questions.question: What does the commitment to continue dialogue actually change?
questions.answer: It preserves a diplomatic channel for discussing security and de-escalation. Without a published operational agreement, it establishes no new ceasefire or military obligations.

articles.impactReason: The spill threatens multiple emirates, marine habitats and coastal activities, while its precise extent remains under assessment.
articles.title: UAE oil slick widens in 24 October satellite images; beaches remain restricted
articles.dek: Cleanup and beach restrictions continue near Umm Al Quwain and Sharjah; the tanker and cause are not officially confirmed.
articles.summary: European Copernicus Sentinel-2 satellite images acquired on 24 October show a widening oil slick off the northern United Arab Emirates. Reuters reported on 26 October that the contamination had spread towards Umm Al Quwain and triggered more coastal restrictions. Local outlets including Gulf News and The National separately covered closures and cleanup measures.
body: European Copernicus Sentinel-2 satellite images acquired on 24 October show a widening oil slick off the northern United Arab Emirates. Reuters reported on 26 October that the contamination had spread towards Umm Al Quwain and triggered more coastal restrictions. Local outlets including Gulf News and The National separately covered closures and cleanup measures.

UAE authorities announced temporary closure of Umm Al Quwain's coastline on 23 October while teams assessed contamination. Sharjah restricted access to Al Hamriyah beach, and Ras Al Khaimah later announced precautionary closures. Restrictions protect visitors and workers while currents and sea conditions can move pollution along the coast.

The spill appears linked to a damaged tanker, but the responsible ministry had not publicly identified the vessel or established the cause. Some maritime specialists suggested a connection to Gem No. 2; that is an attributed identification, not an officially confirmed finding. The existence of an oil slick alone also does not prove a military cause.

The coast supports tourism and marine ecosystems including fish, turtles and corals, and pollution can affect habitats and economic activity. Measuring the damage requires water tests, coastal surveys and estimates of released oil mass. Satellite imagery shows the apparent extent, not the spilled volume by itself. Containment and assessment work continue.
facts: Sentinel-2 images from 24 October show the spread of contamination.
Authorities announced precautionary closures in multiple coastal areas.
perspectives: UAE authorities describe restrictions as precautionary during environmental assessment.
Maritime experts have suggested a specific tanker, though the source is not officially confirmed.
unknowns: The cause, exact vessel, spill volume and measured ecological harm have not been publicly confirmed.

questions.question: What can 24 October Copernicus images establish about the Umm Al Quwain oil slick?
questions.answer: They show its apparent location and extent at the satellite overpass and allow comparison with earlier images; they do not directly measure barrels released or identify the cause.

questions.question: Why were beaches closed beyond the suspected spill origin?
questions.answer: Wind and currents can move oil across different coastal stretches. Precautionary closures limit exposure while authorities assess where contamination has reached.

articles.impactReason: The proposals could reshape French energy policy if enacted, but currently are campaign commitments.
articles.title: Le Pen opens French presidential campaign with proposal to revive oil exploration
articles.dek: At a 25 October rally she promised to repeal the 2017 exploration ban; it remains a political proposal.
articles.summary: Marine Le Pen launched her campaign for France's 2027 presidential election at a Rassemblement National event in Orléans on 25 October. Associated Press and Le Monde reported the address on 26 October, while Reuters examined the broader political messaging. The candidate linked energy policy with wider economic, security and immigration proposals.
body: Marine Le Pen launched her campaign for France's 2027 presidential election at a Rassemblement National event in Orléans on 25 October. Associated Press and Le Monde reported the address on 26 October, while Reuters examined the broader political messaging. The candidate linked energy policy with wider economic, security and immigration proposals.

Le Pen proposed repealing the 2017 law restricting new hydrocarbon exploration permits and shale-gas development. She criticised the law associated with former environment minister Nicolas Hulot and framed renewed exploration as an energy-independence measure. The rally did not itself change any French law.

The debate involves different environmental and economic choices: domestic extraction, import dependence, renewable investment and climate commitments. Assessing possible benefits would require evidence on recoverable resources, development costs and emissions. A promise of more production does not establish that commercially usable reserves have already been proven.

Institutionally, France is preparing to elect a successor to Emmanuel Macron, who cannot seek a third consecutive term. Election results and the future parliamentary balance will determine whether proposals can become law. Le Pen's statements are news about a political platform, not certified forecasts of France's 2027 decisions.
facts: Le Pen held her campaign launch event in Orléans on 25 October.
Her energy proposal targets the 2017 restriction on new exploration permits.
perspectives: Le Pen presents domestic production as part of energy sovereignty.
Critics of new extraction stress climate goals and investment timelines.
unknowns: Commercially recoverable reserves, future parliamentary support and environmental consequences are not established.

questions.question: What change does Le Pen propose to France's 2017 hydrocarbon law?
questions.answer: She wants to permit new oil exploration and related fossil-fuel development currently restricted by the legislation introduced during Nicolas Hulot's ministerial tenure.

questions.question: Would reopening exploration permits immediately guarantee more French oil output?
questions.answer: Exploration, reserve confirmation, approvals, investment and industrial development are distinct steps that can take years and do not guarantee commercial production.

articles.impactReason: Control of the US Congress has international consequences, but this is a campaign development, not an election outcome.
articles.title: US midterms: Trump campaigns in Mississippi as Senate race tightens
articles.dek: The 26 October rally backs Cindy Hyde-Smith against Scott Colom one week before the 3 November vote.
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump travelled to Mississippi on Monday 26 October to campaign for Republican Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith ahead of the 3 November midterm elections. Associated Press and Reuters independently covered the visit and the unusual attention to a normally Republican state. Democratic challenger Scott Colom, a local prosecutor, hopes economic discontent will make the race more competitive.
body: US President Donald Trump travelled to Mississippi on Monday 26 October to campaign for Republican Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith ahead of the 3 November midterm elections. Associated Press and Reuters independently covered the visit and the unusual attention to a normally Republican state. Democratic challenger Scott Colom, a local prosecutor, hopes economic discontent will make the race more competitive.

Republicans are defending narrow congressional control while Democrats seek gains in the House and Senate. Reuters notes that all 435 House seats and 35 of 100 Senate seats are on the ballot. A presidential campaign trip to a normally safe state shows strategic attention, but does not prove which candidate leads.

Trump endorsed Hyde-Smith in his rally and subsequent comments, while Democrats emphasised prices, household costs and the effects of administration policy. Both sides are also focusing on early voting: according to AP, more than 30 million Americans had already voted nationwide. That total does not describe Mississippi alone or ballots cast on rally day.

Midterms do not elect a president, but they can change the government's ability to pass legislation, budgets and appointments. Actual results and local turnout are not yet known. Polling forecasts require attention to fieldwork dates and methods and cannot substitute for certified vote counts.
facts: Trump campaigned for Hyde-Smith in Mississippi on 26 October.
On 3 November voters will choose all 435 House seats and 35 Senate seats.
perspectives: Republicans present Hyde-Smith as an ally of the administration's agenda.
Colom and Democrats focus on economic pressures and checks on the administration.
unknowns: Final seat distribution, local turnout and the degree of competitiveness remain unknown.

questions.question: Why is a presidential rally in Mississippi notable for the 2026 Senate race?
questions.answer: The state usually votes Republican, but the party is devoting resources to defending Hyde-Smith's seat against Colom. The trip signals strategic concern, not a predicted winner.

questions.question: Why don't more than 30 million early ballots already determine the midterm outcome?
questions.answer: That is a nationwide number of ballots cast, not a verified party tally or Mississippi result. Counting and certification in individual states determine the seats.
